parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use integration by parts to find the value of ∫01(2x+1)e−xdx\int_0^1 (2x + 1)e^{-x}\,dx. Show the work that leads to your answer.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine whether the area of RR is finite. If it is, find it; if it is not, explain why. Use correct limit notation throughout.

rubric.point: Improper integral written as a limit: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b \to \infty} \int_0^b (2x + 1)e^{-x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^\infty f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_0^b f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Antiderivative evaluated inside the limit: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b \to \infty}\left(3 - (2b + 3)e^{-b}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

no point for "arithmetic with infinity" such as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-(2\infty + 3)e^{-\infty}</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine whether ∫1∞2xx2+1dx\int_1^\infty \frac{2x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx converges or diverges. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: Limit with the antiderivative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b \to \infty}\left(\ln(b^2 + 1) - \ln 2\right)</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b \to \infty} \ln(x^2 + 1)\Big|_1^b</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Conclusion: diverges, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(b^2 + 1) \to \infty</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: "the limit is infinite, so the integral diverges"
no point for "diverges" without the limit shown

parts.sample: With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^\infty \frac{2x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{b \to \infty} \ln(x^2 + 1)\Big|_1^b</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{b \to \infty}\left(\ln(b^2 + 1) - \ln 2\right)</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(b^2 + 1)</annotation></semantics></math> grows without bound, the limit is infinite and the integral diverges.
